chunks: Sa'd narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him: A man recites aloud in what is not appropriate for reciting aloud, and conceals in what is not appropriate for concealing, and leaves reciting in what is appropriate for reciting, or recites in what is not appropriate for reciting. He said: 'Whatever he did, if he did it forgetfully or negligently, there is no blame upon him.'

And what Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Abu al-Jawza', from al-Husayn ibn Alwan, from Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn Ali (peace be upon him) who said: I prayed Maghrib with my father (peace be upon him), and he forgot the Opening of the Book in the first rak'ah, so he recited it in the second.

key_terms.فَاتِحَةُ الْكِتَابِ: The Opening of the Book (Surah Al-Fatiha)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets to recite Surah Al-Fatiha in the first rak'ah of prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that minor liturgical errors in prayer recitation, such as incorrect volume or omission, incur no penalty if committed out of forgetfulness (nasi) or inattention (sahw), reflecting the Shia principle of leniency in ritual acts. The accompanying report from Zayd ibn Ali illustrates the practical application of this ruling, where the Imam corrected a missed Fatihah by reciting it in the subsequent rak'ah, demonstrating the flexibility within the structure of obligatory prayer. These accounts underscore the scholarly emphasis on intention and ease, distinguishing between intentional deviation and natural human error in worship.
